issues.description: The Book struct in the solution defines the title property as `bookTitle`, but the problem statement specifies the property name `title` and the Client code uses `book.title`. This name mismatch will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct model field name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct's `bookTitle` property to `title` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the problem statement and Client usage (or alternatively update Client and the problem statement consistently). Ensure all usages are updated accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a Book struct with a property named 'title', and the Client usage prints book.title. However, the solution implementation of Book uses the property name 'bookTitle'. This naming divergence (title vs. bookTitle) is the same conceptual field but with different identifiers, causing a direct mapping and compilation confusion for students and breaking the expected initializer/memberwise usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct property 'bookTitle' to 'title' in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the problem statement and Client usage. Ensure the memberwise initializer and all usages are updated accordingly (or use 'title' as the parameter label when initializing Book instances). This aligns the conceptual entity name across problem, implementation, and client code.
